claims.text: Ultrafine-grained MoNbTaW specimens have a higher grain-boundary density than coarse-grained MoNbTaW specimens.
Ultrafine-grained MoNbTaW specimens contain more refined dislocation substructures than coarse-grained specimens.
High-strain deformation followed by low-temperature annealing produces ultrafine grains in MoNbTaW.
An increased grain-boundary density enhances grain-boundary diffusion during high-temperature deformation.
A high density of grain boundaries facilitates dislocation recovery during high-temperature deformation.
Enhanced grain-boundary diffusion and dislocation recovery increase the high-temperature yield strength of ultrafine-grained MoNbTaW.
Enhanced grain-boundary diffusion and dislocation recovery modify the temperature dependence of the elastic modulus.
Coarse-grained MoNbTaW exhibits less diffusion-mediated recovery than ultrafine-grained MoNbTaW.
Coarse-grained and ultrafine-grained MoNbTaW have different local stress distributions.
Ultrafine-grained MoNbTaW will have higher yield strength than the coarse-grained baseline between 800 and 1200 degrees Celsius.
Ultrafine-grained MoNbTaW will exhibit a different elastic-modulus-versus-temperature slope from the coarse-grained baseline.
An inert testing atmosphere minimizes oxidation effects and helps isolate intrinsic high-temperature behavior.
The proposed mechanism may not apply under oxidizing atmospheres or at temperatures substantially outside 800–1200 degrees Celsius.
Additional high-temperature recovery processes could influence the measured mechanical and thermoelastic differences.
No statistically significant yield-strength or thermoelastic difference between the two groups would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe the expected correlation between grain-boundary density or dislocation recovery and the measured property changes would falsify the hypothesis.
